title: Pipeline Perils
summary: crude oil supplies have been under scrutiny for several years as foreign imports have been on the rise not only to meet increased demand, but also to make up for declining production. The crude oil market experienced a bit of a shock this week when BP announced that production out of Prudhoe Bay, Alaska would be significantly reduced for pipline repairs. The initial indications suggested of loss of 400,000 barrels per day of Alaskan North Slope (ANS) crude, but this was later revised downward to about 200,000 per day.

children.title: ANS Field Maintenance
children.summary: The graph on the previous page shows Alaskan crude oil production and VLCC time charter equivalents (TCEs) from the Arabian Gulf to US Gulf on 280,000 MT over the past five years. While the significant run-up in tanker rates at the end of 2004 had several causes, the loss of nearly 300,000 barrels per day was certainly a contributing factor.
